answers.M6-S1: Wanting something badly can make a person believe what they want to hear, so they get fooled easily.
answers.M6-S2: So the narrator won't talk to anyone who could tell him the seed is fake and Billy tricked him out of ten cents.
answers.M6-S3: The narrator thinks Billy is doing him a special favor, but the reader can tell Billy is tricking him into buying worthless seed.
answers.M6-S4: He is secretly worried about being short like Uncle Alec, and Billy is tall, so he believes the seed works.
answers.M6-S5: To make the seed sound mysterious and rare, and to keep the narrator from going to Peg Bowen to check or get more.
answers.M6-S6: It shows the narrator still trusts the seed and makes excuses, which is funny because the reader suspects it will never work.
answers.M6-S7: It explains why the narrator believes Billy's story; Billy's height seems like proof that the seed works.
answers.M6-S8: That Billy wasn't really liked or trusted by people, hinting that he might not be honest with the narrator either.
answers.M6-S9: He cares about Uncle Alec and isn't insulting him, but he doesn't want to end up as short as Uncle Alec is.
